in_hebrew.name: אשכול
in_hebrew.meaning: ענבים, קבוצת ענבים, או אשכול ענבים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אשכול נגזר מהמילה העברית 'אשכול', שפירושה קבוצת ענבים או ענב. הוא מופיע בתנ"ך, בפרשת שלח לך, כשם הנחל בו מצאו המרגלים את הענבים. שם זה נושא משמעות של פריון, שפע וברכה. במסורת היהודית והנוצרית, השם אשכול מייצג את השפע והפריוניות של הארץ המובטחת.

in_greek.name: Αἰσχόλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αἰσχόλ προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή λέξη 'אשכול' (Eshkol), που σημαίνει σύμπλεγμα σταφυλιών ή σταφύλι. Στο Χριστιανισμό και την Ιουδαϊκή παράδοση, το όνομα αυτό συμβολίζει την γονιμότητα, την αφθονία και την ευλογία. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη δεν αναφέρεται συγκεκριμένα, αλλά η ετυμολογία του συνδέεται με την πλούσια σοδειά και την υπόσχεση της γης.

in_latin.name: Eschol
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Eschol is derived from the Hebrew 'אשכול' (Eshkol), meaning a cluster of grapes. This nomenclature carries connotations of fertility, abundance, and divine blessing. In early Christian and Jewish traditions, Eschol symbolizes the promised land's fertility and richness, reflecting God's providence and care.

in_english.name: Eshcol
in_english.long_meaning: The name Eshcol originates from the Hebrew 'אשכול' (Eshkol), signifying a cluster of grapes. It appears in the Bible in the book of Numbers, 13:23, as the name of the valley where the spies found the famous cluster of grapes. Eshcol represents abundance, fertility, and divine blessing in Christian and Jewish traditions. The name symbolizes the richness of the Promised Land and God's promise of provision. It is associated with positive attributes such as fruitfulness, prosperity, and hope.

biblical_reference.note: The name Eshcol is associated with the valley where the Israelites found a cluster of grapes, signifying the fertility of the Promised Land.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eshcol has cultural significance as it is derived from the Hebrew language and biblical traditions. In the Hebrew Bible, the Israelites pass through the Valley of Eshcol after they have conquered the land of Canaan. Here, they celebrate their victory by carrying a large cluster of grapes on a pole, signifying the abundance and prosperity of the land they have conquered. The name Eshcol has also been used in later Jewish traditions and is mentioned in rabbinical writings.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Eshcol lies in its biblical origins, where it symbolizes the promises and blessings of God coming to fruition. In Deuteronomy 1:23-25, the Israelites are reminded of the promise made to their ancestors, and they are encouraged to remember the faithfulness of God in bringing them to the land flowing with milk and honey. The name Eshcol serves as a reminder of God's provision and the fruitfulness of His promises in our own lives. It is also a symbol of the abundance of spiritual blessings that God offers to us, just as a cluster of grapes is a symbol of physical abundance.
